stories.title: Hundreds of thousands still without power after storms hit US on Thanksgiving
summary: Pennsylvania and neighbouring states remain badly affected on Friday after both coasts were lashed with wind and rain.

stories.title: Severe Thanksgiving storms leave roads flooded and trees fallen
summary: Hundreds of thousands of people were without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

stories.title: 'Can't control the weather': Sadness as Macy's Thanksgiving parade postponed
summary: Macy's postpones its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York because of severe weather.

stories.title: The narwhal’s legendary “unicorn horn” holds a remarkable engineering secret
summary: The narwhal’s iconic spiral tusk, once prized in Europe as the horn of a mythical unicorn, conceals an extraordinary feat of natural engineering.
Using advanced X-ray technology, an international team of scientists discovered that the tusk contains two intertwined microscopic spirals that twist in opposite directions.

stories.title: Scientists turn one of the world’s hardest-to-recycle plastics into high-performance lubricating oil
summary: Virginia Tech scientists have discovered how to transform one of the world's hardest-to-recycle plastics into a valuable ingredient for high-performance engine oil.
Their innovative process converts discarded PVC into a useful lubricant material in just three hours.
The breakthrough could turn a major source of plastic pollution into a valuable industrial resource while making lubricant production more sustainable.

stories.title: Floating nature islands installed in parks as Glasgow Games legacy
summary: The islands, being planted in five Glasgow parks, are designed to encourage wildlife and help clean the water.

stories.title: Council to set London's highest littering fines
summary: Fines for littering will rise from £500 to £750 in Harrow, while fly-tipping will see a £5,000 penalty.

stories.title: Major Thanksgiving storm brings flooding, flight delays across US
summary: Almost one million customers in the US had no power on Thursday evening as storms descended on both US coasts, bringing wind gusts, heavy rain and flooding.

stories.title: Watch: Truck hangs in the balance after losing control in wet conditions
summary: A semi-truck carrying mail was left straddling an off-ramp and an overpass in Toledo, Ohio on Thanksgiving Day during severe weather in the US.

stories.title: Scientists identify two ages when children may be most vulnerable to screen time
summary: Scientists have identified two potentially critical periods when screen time may be especially detrimental to children's learning and memory: infancy and the start of formal schooling.
Greater screen exposure during these developmental windows was linked to poorer academic performance and weaker working memory years later.

stories.title: Scientists discover signs of a hidden extinction crisis deep beneath the ocean
summary: The deep sea has long been considered a safe haven for marine life, but new genetic research suggests a hidden biodiversity crisis may be unfolding far beneath the waves.
Scientists analyzing more than a decade of genetic data from five species of deep-sea fish and shrimp in the Gulf discovered troubling signs of extinction risk in every species examined.

stories.title: These bizarre prehistoric mammals may have been misunderstood for 150 years
summary: Giant horned mammals that emerged shortly after the extinction of the dinosaurs may have had far fewer physical differences between males and females than scientists once believed.
The discovery challenges a classic example of sexual dimorphism and raises questions about how historical biases have shaped our understanding of extinct animals.

stories.title: Inside the control room feeding your weather app
summary: BBC Weather's Matt Taylor takes us on a tour of the Met Office control room.

stories.title: Watch: Man and dog narrowly escape powerful king tide in Oregon
summary: Both the man and his dog escaped unharmed, the police department says.

stories.title: For decades, scientists may have misunderstood how brain cells work
summary: A major new study challenges a long-standing assumption about how the brain works, revealing that most neurons are versatile multitaskers rather than highly specialized workers.

By analyzing recordings from 43 regions of the mouse brain, researchers discovered that although some neurons are dedicated to specific functions, most respond to a wide variety of information in remarkably distinct ways.

stories.title: BBC Inside Science
summary: One of the greatest problems in the history of mathematics has been solved by AI.

stories.title: Second court defeat for Trump's deep-sea mining ambitions
summary: Second judge rules against Trump administration's plans to lease areas of ocean floor and survey for mining.

stories.title: Fireball steals the show during Thanksgiving drone display in Indiana
summary: The glowing object was captured on video as holiday-themed drones illuminated the night sky.

stories.title: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men
summary: Men and women appear to be similarly capable of multitasking, but men are more than twice as likely to ignore conversation while juggling multiple activities.
Researchers believe this unexpected difference may help explain why women are widely perceived as better multitaskers.

stories.title: Deep beneath Australia, hidden caves could unlock the secrets of alien worlds
summary: Scientists have solved the mystery of strange trenches scattered across Australia’s vast Nullarbor Plain, revealing an extensive hidden world beneath the surface.
These subtle landscape features are created as deeply buried cave systems slowly collapse upward over millions of years.
The discovery could help researchers locate unexplored caves containing ancient environmental records and unusual life forms.

stories.title: This 345-million-year-old fossil had scientists fooled for decades
summary: A famous 345-million-year-old fossil has turned out to be something entirely different from what scientists believed for decades.
Advanced X-ray imaging revealed hidden gills and thousands of tiny teeth, exposing a primitive aquatic or amphibious creature rather than an early reptile.
The discovery suggests that several adaptations associated with life on land actually evolved in animals still dependent on water.

stories.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
summary: Officials say no lead has been detected in the surrounding area, which continues to be tested following concerns from locals.
